This matter is taken up by hybrid mode.

3. The Petitioner has filed this writ petition with the following prayer:
"Under these circumstances the petitioner most humbly prays that this Hon'ble Court be graciously pleased to admit the writ petition and issue Rule NISI calling upon the opp. parties to show cause as to why- (i) letters No. 1626 dated 26.04.2017 under Annexure- 1 and passed by the Estate Manager, MCL, Kaniha Area, Kaniha as illegal and contrary to Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 shall not be quashed as illegal and without jurisdiction.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: (ii) the opp. parties No. 3 and 4 had issued the letter and the amount mentioned in the letter is not in consonance with the provisions mentioned in Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: (iii) the action of the opp. parties shall not be declared as illegal, arbitrary and unreasonable.

(iv) direct the opp. parties to release the compensation amount in favour of the Purna Chandra Sahoo vs State Of Odisha And Others ..... ... on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11063567/
1 petitioner in terms of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, Act, 2013.
(v) direct the opp. parties No. 3 and 4 to give employment to the petitioner by giving the resettlement and rehabilitation benefits and cost and compensation of the buildings.
And if the opp. parties fail to show cause or show insufficient cause to make the said Rule NISI be absolute.

entities.text: Purna Chandra Sahoo vs State Of Odisha And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And pass any other order/orders as would be deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.
And for the said act of kindness, the petitioner shall as in duty bound ever pray"

4. In course of hearing, learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner states that the Petitioner has already made representation before the Opposite Party No.2 vide Annexure-5, and the same may be directed to be disposed of within a stipulated time, to which learned Counsel for the State has no objection.
5.

As agreed by learned counsel for the parties and after going through the records, this Court,
without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, disposes of the Writ Petition directing Opposite Party No.2 to consider and dispose of the representation filed by the Petitioner vide Annexure-5 and pass appropriate order as early as possible within a period of three months from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
